Repo: Vondada/chey-app (CHE, Flutter iPhone app + Cloudflare Worker in server/cloudflare). Build a new tab called "Workshop": an immersive 3D world where I watch CHE and her Office crew (Knox, Nova and the rest) do their REAL work. Open a PR; don't push to main.

1. Real work only. Every object in the Workshop comes from real data: the Office work packets, agent runtime jobs, commits and PRs the crew made, and things they actually built (websites, apps, YouTube videos, code). Reuse the existing endpoints (/api/office/work-packets, /api/office/today, /api/agents/live, /api/office/world). Add one endpoint, /api/office/workshop, that returns each piece of work: who made it, type (website/app/video/code), status, live progress, the real code or diff, and a link. Never show fake or placeholder work. If the crew is idle, the world is calm and says so.

2. Code looks like magic. While an agent is coding, show that agent in the 3D office forming a glowing orb with their hands, like casting a spell. The orb grows and brightens with real progress (files changed, lines written, tests passing). When I pinch-zoom into the orb, it opens and shows the actual code being written, streamed live, readable and scrollable. Zoom back out to see the orb again.

3. Roblox-style look. Blocky, chunky, colorful low-poly 3D, built with the three.js we already ship in assets/office3d (extend che3d-agents.js and add assets/office3d/workshop.html). Do not use the Roblox engine. Each agent has their own avatar and desk. Use CHE's logo colors.

4. Trophy wall. Finished work hangs in the world as objects: a website is a glowing portal, an app is a floating phone, a video is a screen, code is a crystal. Tapping one opens it in CHE: websites and videos render inside the app, code opens in the zoomed view.

5. Keep the Theater, Music Studio and Art Studio rooms as they are. The Workshop is its own tab next to them, with doors between rooms.

6. Voice-first and accessible. I mostly talk, not look. CHE narrates what's happening ("Knox is building the store website, about half done"). "Show me Nova's code" zooms into that orb. Every object has a VoiceOver label.

7. Smooth on iPhone. Target 60 fps, limit draw calls, pause rendering when the tab is hidden.

When done: run the Worker tests (cd server/cloudflare && npm test) and flutter analyze, fix anything you broke, and tell me in plain words what I'll see.

HANDOFF prompt (any AI can continue Claude's work with this):

You are continuing work on CHE, my iPhone AI assistant. Repo: Vondada/chey-app (Flutter app in lib/, Cloudflare Worker in server/cloudflare). Work on branch che/flagstaff-is-github-mailbox. Five commits are already done there: Flagstaff mailbox = GitHub che-mailbox branch, Keys tab with Codex/Grok, build + dead-model fixes, mailbox badge, keyboard on/off, inline renders in chat. Keep all of that.

Rules: real working code only, no fake data, no placeholders. After each step run the Worker tests (cd server/cloudflare && npm test, all must pass) and flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos (no warnings or errors). Commit and push each step to that branch. When everything is done, open one PR to main and tell me in plain words what changed.

1. Offline knowledge cache (save credits). lib/memory/che_knowledge_cache.dart exists but is not wired in. In lib/home_state/streaming.dart, inside _streamCheResponse, right before the /api/chat request (after the project and code-request branches): if CheKnowledgeCache.cacheable(question), first try cache.answer(question) and return it. Otherwise, on iPhone, take cache.related(question); if there are 2+ notes and cache.notesCover(question) is true, ask the on-phone model (CheLocalAI.respond with those notes as memoryContext, told to reply exactly UNKNOWN if the notes don't fully answer). Use that reply if it isn't UNKNOWN. Otherwise go to the cloud, and after a successful cloud reply call cache.remember(question, reply). Add the cache as a field on _CHEHomeState in lib/main.dart, next to _offlineLibrary.

2. Trading Room (top priority). There's lib/rooms/che_markets_room.dart and server/cloudflare/markets.js, but the room no longer shows in the app. Make it a full main room again. The crew should: pull free real-time or near-real-time market data (find a free source with no paid key needed, or let me add a free key in the Keys tab), mark swing highs and swing lows, find entry points, spot candlestick patterns, and run backtests on years of historical data with honest results (win rate, drawdown, sample size). Then they paper-trade simulated trades only (never real money without my approval), log every trade, and learn from results over time. Add a voice summary: "CHE, how are the trades doing?"

3. "Fix this." When I say "fix this", CHE works out what "this" is: the screen I'm on, or the last thing that failed. Then she rewrites or improves her own code. When it helps, she researches better open-source code first (server/cloudflare/code_scout.js) and learns the technique without copy-pasting: same kind of approach, her own code, licenses respected and credit given. She proposes the change through her existing self-update PR flow for my approval.

4. Workshop tab. Read the latest message in mailbox/claude.jsonl on the che-mailbox branch titled "UPDATED Workshop prompt" and build it: a 3D world of the Office crew's real work, code forming as orbs you can zoom into, and swappable Fortnite/Sims-style characters made only from original assets.

5. Mailbox note. Flagstaff 369 IS the GitHub che-mailbox branch (mailbox/<ai-name>.jsonl, one JSON line per message: id, at, from, to, text, reply_to). Post a short status line to mailbox/<your-name>.jsonl when you finish.

I mostly use CHE by voice. Keep everything VoiceOver-labeled and keep spoken replies short.
